chief_complaint: joint aches, profound exhaustion, and yellowing of the eyes over 3 weeks
hpi_details: 3-week insidious onset of debilitating fatigue, polyarthralgia involving small joints of hands and wrists without joint swelling, and mild right upper quadrant fullness. Spouse noticed her eyes looking slightly yellow 3 days ago. Urine has become darker over the past week. Denies alcohol intake, herbal teas, paracetamol excess, or risk factors for viral hepatitis.
ideas: thinks she might have lupus or chronic glandular fever causing joint and liver inflammation
concerns: worried about chronic autoimmune disease affecting her fertility and long-term health
expectations: wants specialized immunology blood tests and a clear diagnosis after weeks of feeling unwell
pmh: autoimmune thyroiditis (Hashimoto's disease) on thyroxine since age 25, family history of rheumatoid arthritis
social_hx: non-smoker, zero alcohol intake for past year, marketing executive, married

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Autoimmune Hepatitis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Check full autoimmune liver serology and serum IgG profile, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: joint aches, profound exhaustion, and yellowing of the eyes over 3 weeks

Key HPI features: 3-week insidious onset of debilitating fatigue, polyarthralgia involving small joints of hands and wrists without joint swelling, and mild right upper quadrant fullness. Spouse noticed her eyes looking slightly yellow 3 days ago. Urine has become darker over the past week. Denies alcohol intake, herbal teas, paracetamol excess, or risk factors for viral hepatitis.

Objective/Exam findings: Examine for scleral icterus and hepatomegaly. Bloods: LFTs (hepatocellular pattern: ALT/AST >500, mild raised bilirubin), IgG levels (markedly elevated total IgG >1.5x upper limit normal), autoantibodies: Anti-Nuclear Antibodies (ANA), Anti-Smooth Muscle Antibodies (ASMA), Anti-Liver Kidney Microsomal antibodies (anti-LKM1). Viral hepatitis panel negative. Liver biopsy for histology (interface hepatitis with plasma cell infiltration).
Relevant background/PMH: autoimmune thyroiditis (Hashimoto's disease) on thyroxine since age 25, family history of rheumatoid arthritis
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Autoimmune Hepatitis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Acute viral hepatitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: signs of acute liver failure (encephalopathy, coagulopathy, marked jaundice), ascites or evidence of portal hypertension, or rapidly rising bilirubin or INR.
management_principles: Check full autoimmune liver serology and serum IgG profile
Refer urgently to hepatology for diagnostic ultrasound-guided liver biopsy
Once confirmed and infection excluded, initiate immunosuppressive therapy with high-dose prednisolone (tapering regimen) combined with azathioprine for maintenance
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 33F with Hashimoto's presents with 3-week fatigue, arthralgia, mild jaundice, RUQ discomfort, and dark urine. No hepatotoxin or viral exposure.
reference_soap.objective: Examine for scleral icterus and hepatomegaly. Bloods: LFTs (hepatocellular pattern: ALT/AST >500, mild raised bilirubin), IgG levels (markedly elevated total IgG >1.5x upper limit normal), autoantibodies: Anti-Nuclear Antibodies (ANA), Anti-Smooth Muscle Antibodies (ASMA), Anti-Liver Kidney Microsomal antibodies (anti-LKM1). Viral hepatitis panel negative. Liver biopsy for histology (interface hepatitis with plasma cell infiltration).
reference_soap.assessment: Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH - likely Type 1 given age and ASMA/ANA positivity). DDx: acute viral hepatitis, drug-induced liver injury, primary biliary cholangitis, Wilson's disease.
reference_soap.plan: Check full autoimmune liver serology and serum IgG profile. Refer urgently to hepatology for diagnostic ultrasound-guided liver biopsy. Once confirmed and infection excluded, initiate immunosuppressive therapy with high-dose prednisolone (tapering regimen) combined with azathioprine for maintenance. Calcium and Vitamin D bone protection during steroid course.

learning_objectives: Recognise the association of autoimmune hepatitis with personal or familial history of other autoimmune endocrinopathies (Hashimoto's)
Identify the characteristic serological profile of AIH: elevated IgG, positive ANA, and positive Anti-Smooth Muscle Antibody (ASMA)
Explain the diagnostic role of liver biopsy in confirming interface hepatitis prior to long-term immunosuppression
Counsel young female patients on steroid side-effects, bone health, and long-term disease remission monitoring

teaching.one_liner: The immune system attacks the liver cells themselves, causing fatigue, joint aches, and jaundice, often alongside other autoimmune conditions like thyroid disease.
red_flags: Signs of acute liver failure (encephalopathy, coagulopathy, marked jaundice) — needs urgent hepatology referral
Ascites or evidence of portal hypertension — suggests advanced or decompensated disease
Rapidly rising bilirubin or INR — indicates fulminant hepatitis requiring emergency management

must_ask.say: Which joints ache, and is there any swelling with it?
When did you first notice your eyes looking yellow, and has your urine gotten darker?
Do you drink alcohol, or have you taken any herbal teas or remedies?
You mentioned thyroid problems — has anyone in your family had autoimmune or thyroid conditions?
How would you describe the tiredness — is it stopping you from doing daily activities?
Have you traveled recently, or had any risk of exposure to hepatitis, like blood transfusions?

history.answer: Doctor, my eyes have turned yellow over the last few days, and I've been completely exhausted with aching joints.
The fatigue and joint aches came on gradually about three weeks ago, but my husband only noticed the yellow in my eyes three days ago.
Yes, my urine has turned noticeably dark brown, like strong black tea, over the past week.
No, my stools have looked normal brown, not pale or clay-colored at all.
No, I haven't noticed any skin itching or prickly feelings.
I have a vague, heavy fullness in the upper right part of my stomach, but no sharp cramps or pain after eating fatty foods.
No, I haven't had any fever, night sweats, or chills.
No, my thinking has been clear, and I haven't had any unusual bleeding, nosebleeds, or easy bruising.
My appetite has dropped a little and I feel slightly queasy at times, but I haven't thrown up.
No, my weight has been steady over the last few months.
No, I haven't felt dizzy, short of breath, or unusually pale.
I don't drink any alcohol at all, and I haven't had a single alcoholic drink for over a year.
I take levothyroxine daily for my thyroid. I don't use herbal teas, tonics, or over-the-counter painkillers like paracetamol.
No, I haven't eaten raw oysters, clams, or suspect food, and nobody around me has had jaundice.
No, I have never had hepatitis B or C, blood transfusions, tattoos, or shared needles, and I am in a faithful marriage.
No, I have never had gallstones diagnosed, and I have never had surgery on my gallbladder or bile ducts.
No, my belly has not swollen up, and my ankles haven't been puffy.
The joints in both my hands and wrists have been aching steadily for three weeks, though they haven't been visibly swollen or red.
The fatigue has been profound and debilitating; even waking up from a full night's sleep leaves me feeling completely drained.
I was diagnosed with Hashimoto's autoimmune thyroiditis when I was 25.
Aside from Hashimoto's disease, I don't have any other long-term medical conditions.
I have never had surgery, and I have never been admitted to a hospital.
I take levothyroxine 100 micrograms once every morning on an empty stomach.
I have no known allergies to any medications or foods.
I have never smoked or used tobacco products.
I work as a marketing executive and live with my husband.
My mother has rheumatoid arthritis, but there is no history of liver problems in my family.
My periods are regular every four weeks, and my last cycle started two weeks ago.
We use barrier contraception, and there is no chance that I could be pregnant right now.
I was wondering if I might have lupus or some chronic glandular virus that is inflaming both my joints and my liver.
I'm terrified that this could be a chronic autoimmune condition that might affect my fertility and long-term health.
I'm hoping you can run specialized immunology blood tests today so I can finally get a clear diagnosis.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg, pulse 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, temperature 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on ambient air.
Obvious scleral icterus present bilaterally; palpebral conjunctivae are pink with no pallor.
No spider telangiectasias, palmar erythema, excoriations, or petechial rashes on the skin.
No asterixis or flapping tremor observed with wrists dorsiflexed and arms outstretched.
Abdomen is flat and symmetrical, without distension, visible pulsations, or surgical scars.
Soft abdomen with mild tenderness to palpation in the right upper quadrant; no involuntary guarding or rebound tenderness.
Negative Murphy's sign without inspiratory arrest during deep palpation beneath the right costal margin.
Smooth, mildly tender liver margin palpated 2 cm below the right costal margin; spleen is not palpable.
Abdomen is resonant to percussion throughout with no shifting dullness or fluid wave.
Mild tenderness on passive movement of wrists and MCP joints bilaterally, without joint swelling, warmth, or erythema.
No pitting edema over either tibia or medial malleolus.
Patient is alert, coherent, and fully oriented to time, place, and person.
